scope: Thin cellulose fuel in QUIESCENT microgravity at 1 atm. Fitted on the two thicknesses Olson flew. Not validated for forced flow, other materials, other pressures, or thicknesses outside the two below.
data_source: NTRS 19880006471 (NASA TM-100195) Appendix A Tables A-I and A-III
near_limit_definition: oxygen <= 30 %, where a fire-safety tool must be right
why_not: Fitted on 21-100 % O2, quiescent (flow 0), thin cellulose at 1 atm. FLARE-X operates at 14.2-31 % O2 with forced flow 1-25 cm/s on PMMA rods and fabrics. 70 % of FLARE-X rows sit below 21 % O2 and none are quiescent, so using this model there would extrapolate on oxygen, flow and fuel at once.
caveat: R2 0.9038 is driven by the high-oxygen points where spread rates are large. Mean relative error is 31 % overall and 54 % below 30 % O2. A free power law fits the near-limit region better (34 % relative error) but only reaches R2 0.51, and its oxygen exponent is 1.70 rather than the published 0.9 because Olson is quiescent while the 0.9 correlation is opposed-flow.
